annotations.title: Is this dependence on one customer high or normal for its peers?

description: Use when the user is pricing customer-concentration risk in a deal or asks whether a target’s reliance on one customer (often Walmart) is unusual: "our target gets 32% from Walmart, is that high for food companies?". Returns each peer’s largest-customer share of revenue from its latest 10-K XBRL, the peer median and range, and where the target sits. Peers that tag no figure are listed as unknown, never zero. Refuses before you are charged if fewer than two peers can be measured. Every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. Calling this tool returns a quote, not the result: what the run measures, its price and a payment_url. The run happens only when you POST to payment_url, and a run that fails its controls refuses there with nothing charged. Dimensions (vary these inputs to cut the answer; each call is its own run): over time: one release (latest 10-Ks); compare: peers. Price: $0.05 per run over x402 (USDC on Base, no account needed), or $0.50 over MPP (a Stripe shared payment token); charged only when the run comes back sound. For one company’s largest customer over three years, use run_customer_concentration.

peers.description: 2-6 peer tickers, comma-separated, from: PEP, KO, K, POST, KDP, CELH, UTZ, HRL, GIS, KHC, CAG, CPB, HSY, MDLZ, SJM, CLX, CL, CHD, PG, SMPL, BRBR, MSFT, EA, TTWO, RBLX, OMC, STGW, CRM, HUBS, TDOC, TALK, GDDY, GEN, NFLX, AMZN, DKNG, FLUT, CHDN, PENN, RSI, MSGK, BATRA, TKO, LYV, SPHR, MSGE.

target_share.description: Optional: a private target’s largest customer as a percent of revenue, from its own books. Not with ticker.

ticker.description: Optional: a public company from the same list to place against the peers. Not with target_share.
